summary: This note describes the 2017 World Series, the championship series of Major League Baseball's 2017 season and the 113th edition of the event. It was a best-of-seven series played October 24 to November 1 between the National League champion Los Angeles Dodgers and the American League champion Houston Astros, sponsored by YouTube TV. The excerpt focuses on the opening game, highlighting Chris Taylor's leadoff home run, Justin Turner's go-ahead blast, and Clayton Kershaw's strong pitching performance.
one_line: The 2017 World Series, MLB's 2017 championship best-of-seven series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Houston Astros.
key_facts: The 2017 World Series was the championship series of Major League Baseball's (MLB) 2017 season.
It was the 113th edition of the World Series.
The series was played between October 24 and November 1, 2017.
The series was a best-of-seven playoff between the National League (NL) champion Los Angeles Dodgers and the American League (AL) champion Houston Astros.
The series was sponsored by the Internet television service YouTube TV and officially known as the World Series presented by YouTube TV.
Chris Taylor hit a home run for the Dodgers on Keuchel's first pitch of the game.
Chris Taylor's home run was the third leadoff home run in Dodgers postseason history, following Davey Lopes in 1978 and Carl Crawford in 2013 NLDS.
Alex Bregman hit a tying solo home run for the Astros in the fourth inning.
Justin Turner hit a go-ahead two-run home run for the Dodgers in the sixth inning.
Justin Turner tied Duke Snider for most career runs batted in (RBIs) in Dodgers postseason history with 26.
Kershaw struck out 11 in seven innings pitched with no walks and only three hits allowed.
Keuchel allowed three runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Brandon Morrow pitched a scoreless eighth inning and Kenley Jansen earned the save.
The two-hour, 28-minute game was the shortest World Series contest since Game 4 in 1992.
